PSF-based Multiple Scattering Rendering approximates volumetric light transport by convolving a vacuum-rendered image with a spatially varying Gaussian Point Spread Function (PSF) derived from the medium's optical properties [S3, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the method (Elek et al. [2013]) is based on 'image filtering of the input image L that was rendered in a vacuum' (Source [S3], Section 3.1). It further details that a 'blurring point spread function' (PSF) is derived and applied to approximate light transport. The formula for the standard deviation $W(s)$ of this Gaussian PSF is provided, showing it depends on optical properties ($σ_a, σ_s, g$) and distance $s$, making it spatially varying. The final equation $L' = L_{at} + G * L_{sc}$ confirms the convolution (blurring) of the scattered component with the Gaussian PSF.
